newsitem.title: UK: Loftus Road seeks Premiership status for QPR.
newsitem.headline: Loftus Road seeks Premiership status for QPR.

text.p: Loftus Road Plc's immediate aims are to secure promotion for its football club to the Premier League and capitalise on the success of its rugby club, the company's chairman said on Wednesday.
Loftus Road is the holding company for Queens Park Rangers Football Club and Wasps Rugby Football Club.

Once these objectives are reached "the financial performance of the Group should improve considerably," Chris Wright said in a statement accompanying its first results since admission to the Alternative Investment Market in October 1996.

The interim results covered the period of May 13, 1996 to November 30, 1996 and showed a pretax loss of 4.4 million stg. There was a trading loss of 1.5 million stg before net transfer fees payable of 2.9 million stg.

The results include exceptional costs of around 537,000 stg in total arising from changes in the management at QPR, marketing rugby for the first time and work connected with the acquisitions and reorganisation of businesses.
The company does not intend to pay a dividend in the year to May 31, 1997, believing it is in the group's interest to retain cash to fund further expansion.

"The management of both clubs will keep their playing squads under constant review and will continue to seek new players to strengthen the sides which will also be developed over time by increased investment in our youth policies," Wright said.

The flotation of Loftus Road on AIM in October 1996 raised a net 11.9 million stg, of which 4.0 million stg was used to repay bridging finance raised to complete funding of the acquisitions of the two clubs.
The company said it had made good progress in its search for a chief executive and expects an appointment to be announced before the end of the financial year.
